knowledge_gaps: The proposed comparison changes witness eligibility, denominator normalization and norm clipping together. Improvement over the previous residual would not isolate independent-witness support. A matched residual with identical normalization, clipping and recency but no witness requirement is needed; a popularity-matched text shuffle would help distinguish lexical evidence from frequency shortcuts.

Witness availability is unmeasured. Two distinct witnesses separated by three positions require at least four retained events, and meaningful lexical overlap may be rare. Report eligible-prefix frequency, nonzero confidence, residual-to-base norm and gate values by dataset and history length before interpreting a null result.

Different item identities and positional separation do not establish independent evidence. Duplicate descriptions, brand boilerplate and related product variants can satisfy the rule. Moreover, max–min confidence selects the strongest pair rather than accumulating repeated support, and older witnesses can sustain a recent anchor because only the anchor receives recency decay.

Implementation feasibility remains unresolved. Blocking reduces intermediate memory but does not itself reduce arithmetic complexity. Specify an exact incremental witness algorithm, sparse text-similarity computation, peak memory and accounted runtime. Validate against brute-force results on short sequences.

Reproduction details remain incomplete: the decoded tokenizer regex needs verification; title/description concatenation, embedding scaling, gate scope, checkpoint cadence, tie handling, actual remaining GPU budget and per-arm allocation need explicit values. No validation HR@10 results or uncertainty estimates establish improvement yet.

Originality 4/10 is appropriately cautious, but potential 7/10 remains speculative and difficulty 5/10 may understate exact causal computation and deployment work. HGN and HAM should be compared directly alongside text-based methods. Training-prefix causality must also be distinguished from causal inference about user preferences.
